Yes, expression of c-kit protooncogene has been observed in various stages of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). C-kit positivity was found in mitotic, proliferating, and dysplastic hepatic cells, suggesting that it may serve as an early diagnostic indicator for HBV-induced HCC.

This means that researchers believe c-kit expression could potentially help identify patients with liver cancer at an earlier stage. However, more studies are needed to confirm this finding and validate its role in diagnosing HBV-related HCC.

It's essential to note that the accuracy of imaging methods, such as MRI or CT scans, will become less effective when laparoscopic staging (SL) is used for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. Additional percutaneous liver biopsy may be recommended in these cases to further confirm the diagnosis.

As a result, clinicians should consider c-kit expression positivity when evaluating patients with HBV-related HCC and monitor them closely during treatment to assess its potential impact on patient outcomes.

While this is a promising area of research, more studies are required to fully understand the role of c-kit in diagnosing HBV-induced HCC.
